title: Email Communications Related to Real Time Information Center

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: Email Communications Related to Real Time Information Center
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

(1) All sent and received emails from the email account of Senior Commander Ryan Murphy of the Saint Paul Police Department related to the city's Real Time Information Center including but not limited to the following terms: "Real Time Information Center", "RTIC", "Axon Fusus", "Fusus", "Axon Fusus Community Connect" and "Community Connect". Please include all emails and attached documents from January 1, 2025 through the date of this request. 

(2) All sent and received emails from the email account of Deputy Chief Kurt Hallstrom of the Saint Paul Police Department related to the city's Real Time Information Center including but not limited to the following terms: "Real Time Information Center", "RTIC", "Axon Fusus", "Fusus", "Axon Fusus Community Connect" and "Community Connect". Please include all emails and attached documents from January 1, 2025 through the date of this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Eyes Off Saint Paul

title: Public records request — online driver-license renewal photo failures, customer notices, and handling fees

communications.subject: Nebraska Public Records Act Request: Public records request — online driver-license renewal photo failures, customer notices, and handling fees
communications.communication:
Dear Public Records Custodian:

Pursuant to the Nebraska Public Records Statutes, Neb. Rev. Stat. § 84-712 et seq., I request copies of the following existing records held by the Nebraska Department of Motor Vehicles concerning online driver-license renewals for the period January 1st, 2026 through the date of this request:

1. Incident, problem, change, or implementation records concerning photographs that could not be retrieved, transferred, or used to complete an online driver-license renewal, including records identifying when the problem began, when it was discovered, its cause, the affected transactions, and any remediation.

2. Policies, procedures, scripts, bulletins, or other instructions to staff concerning how to handle affected customers, including whether they must appear in person, whether their online renewal payment is credited, and whether an expiring temporary license or receipt may be extended.

3. Notices, emails, letters, website messages, or other communications sent or prepared for affected customers concerning the photo problem, an incomplete renewal, a required in-person visit, or the status of their temporary document. For each form of notice, please provide existing records showing when it was used and how many customers received it, if those records exist.

4. Existing reports or exportable aggregate data showing, by week and by applicant county of residence, the number of online driver-license renewals submitted; completed; delayed, held, or rejected because a photograph was unavailable; and subsequently completed in person. Please include the applicable transaction-status and error-code definitions. If the DMV does not maintain county-level figures, please provide the statewide figures and any existing geographic breakdown. Please also provide the number of online driver-license renewal attempts during each reporting week, by applicant county of residence, so the rate of photo-related failures can be calculated using the same time period, geography, and transaction population. If the data distinguishes unique applicants from attempts or retries, please provide both counts and identify which measure is used for each status. Please include any existing county-level counts of completed online renewals and in-person renewals for the same period.

5. Policies, procedures, system documentation, or staff guidance concerning credits or refunds of online renewal payments and online handling fees when a customer must instead complete the renewal in person because the DMV cannot access or use the customer’s photograph. Please include records describing any technical limitation on refunding the handling fee.

6. Existing aggregate reports or exportable counts showing how many customers affected by the photograph issue paid an online handling fee that was not refunded, and the total amount of those retained fees. If no report identifies that specific group, please provide existing reports or data showing handling fees collected and refunded for online driver-license renewals during the requested period, with definitions needed to interpret those figures.

I seek administrative records and aggregate data, not individual driver records, photographs, license numbers, names, addresses, or other personal information. Please redact personal information where necessary and release reasonably segregable portions of responsive records.

Please provide records electronically in their existing format where practicable, including CSV or spreadsheet files for existing tabular data. I am requesting existing records and exports, not asking the Department to create a new analysis. If you anticipate fees, please provide an itemized estimate before incurring them. If the Department does not hold a requested category of records, please identify that category so I can direct a follow-up request to the appropriate custodian.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 4 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jeff Geiger
